Staying at Maimuna's, Ibn Abbas stood on the Prophet's left in the night prayer, and the Prophet took him by his locks of hair and moved him to his right.
The Prophet forbade Al-Qaza', shaving a boy's head while leaving tufts of hair here and there, as Nafi' explained.
Aisha perfumed the Prophet with her own hands for Ihram and at Mina before Tawaf al-Ifada, with the best scent, until its shine showed on his head and beard.
A man peeped through a hole as the Prophet combed his head; had he known, the Prophet said, he would have pierced his eye, as asking permission prevents unlawful looking.
Aisha combed the Prophet's hair during her periods, and he liked to start from the right in combing and in ablution.
Allah says fasting is for Him and He rewards it, and the smell of a fasting person's mouth is better to Allah than musk.
Aisha perfumed the Prophet with the best scent before Ihram, and with Dharira at the Farewell Hajj on entering and leaving it, and he never refused a gift of scent.
Allah cursed women who tattoo, remove facial hair, gap their teeth or add false hair, or have it done, false hair being refused even for a bride who lost hers.
The Prophet forbade tattooing and cursed women who tattoo, are tattooed or lengthen hair, as he forbade usury and the price of blood or a dog; Umar asked about it.
Angels do not enter a house with a dog or pictures; picture-makers face the severest punishment and must give life to their work, and the Prophet tore Aisha's pictured curtain.
Aisha added that she and the Prophet used to bathe from one container.
Seeing Aisha's pictured cushion the Prophet would not enter, saying picture-makers must give life to their work and angels avoid such houses, though a design on a garment is excepted.
The Prophet shared his mount: Usama rode behind him on a donkey, and at Mecca he took boys of Bani Abdul Muttalib, Qutham and Al-Fadl, one before and one behind.
Riding behind the Prophet, Mu'adh was told that Allah's right on His slaves is that they worship Him alone, and theirs on Him is that He will not punish them.
Coming from Khaibar, the camel carrying the Prophet and a wife slipped; Anas resaddled it, and nearing Medina the Prophet said they return repentant, worshipping and praising their Lord.
Abbad's uncle saw the Prophet lying down in the mosque with one leg placed over the other.
Dutifulness to parents, mother first, is among the best deeds, serving them a jihad; cursing them is a great sin, and a cave-trapped man invoked his care for them.
The greatest sins are joining partners with Allah, undutifulness to parents and killing a soul, and the Prophet warned repeatedly against a forged statement or false witness.
Asma asked whether she might be kind to her pagan mother, who came during the peace pact hoping for her favour, and the Prophet said yes.
Keeping ties of kinship leads to Paradise, more wealth and longer life, and severing them bars Paradise; the womb sought Allah's refuge, and the true keeper restores ties others cut.
The Prophet let little Um Khalid play with his Prophethood seal, called Hasan and Husain his flowers, carried Umamah in prayer and kissed Al-Hasan; well-treated daughters shield from Fire.
Allah is more merciful to His slaves than a captive mother to her child, and of mercy's hundred parts He sent one to earth, by which creatures show mercy.
The greatest sins are setting up a rival to Allah, killing one's son lest he share one's food, and illegal intercourse with a neighbour's wife, and a verse confirmed it.
A child the Prophet gave Tahnik urinated on him, and he poured water over it; he held Usama and Al-Hasan on his thighs and prayed for mercy on them.
Aisha was jealous of no woman as of Khadija, for the Prophet often mentioned her, was told to promise her a palace in Paradise, and sent meat to her friends.
The Prophet said he and the one who looks after an orphan will be in Paradise like his two joined fingers.
One who looks after and works for a widow and a poor person is like a fighter in Allah's Cause, or one who fasts by day and prays all night.
Sensing young men staying twenty nights missed their families, the kind-hearted Prophet sent them home to teach them, pray as he prayed, give the Adhan and let the eldest lead.
A thirsty man who went down a well again to water a panting dog was forgiven by Allah, and there is reward for serving any living being.
A bedouin who prayed for mercy on himself and Muhammad alone was told by the Prophet that he had narrowed something vast, meaning Allah's Mercy.
Believers in their mercy, love and kindness to one another are like one body: when one part is ill, the whole body shares its sleeplessness and fever.
If a Muslim plants something and a person or an animal eats of it, he is rewarded as if he had given it in charity.
Whoever is not merciful to others will not be treated mercifully, the Prophet said.
Gabriel urged kindness to neighbours till the Prophet thought they would inherit; one whose neighbour fears his harm lacks faith; gifts go to the nearest door, and guests are honoured.
Every Muslim owes charity, by working, helping the distressed, enjoining good or refraining from evil, and the Fire is warded off even with half a date or a kind word.
When Jews wished the Prophet death and Aisha cursed them, he said Allah loves kindness in all matters; he let a bedouin urinating in the mosque finish.
A believer to a believer is like a building whose parts support each other, and the Prophet told them to help and recommend the needy for a reward.
The Prophet, brave and generous, never spoke obscenely or refused requests, urged Aisha to gentleness and was polite to a man he called evil; the best have the best character.
The Prophet said time will pass quickly, good deeds will decrease, miserliness will be cast into hearts, and Harj, meaning killing, will increase.
Anas served the Prophet ten years without ever hearing a word of impatience or blame, and at home the Prophet served his family until prayer time.
